evidence: Three top-level packages (models, misc, docs) with clear separation of concerns: models for core architecture, misc for utilities, docs for documentation
High average fan-out (4.73) indicates tight internal coupling across modules, typical of monolithic designs where modules freely depend on each other
No external communication patterns (e.g., no message queues, REST/gRPC endpoints, or service discovery mechanisms)
Single entry points (train.py, validate.py, export_model.py) that orchestrate the core models and utilities
Shared dependencies (e.g., models.fastvit imports models.modules.mobileone and models.modules.replknet)
Directory depth of 3 suggests hierarchical but single-process organization without network boundaries
All code resides in one repository with no indication of separate deployments or service boundaries
risks: Tight coupling between modules may reduce testability and maintainability over time
Monolithic deployment model limits scalability and fault isolation
Shared state and dependencies across modules could increase regression risk during updates
